topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I walked past the old spot this afternoon, the very place I once cherished as a secret no one else knew. There, where the ground had always seemed a little softer, where the sun seemed to shine just a bit brighter, now stands not a towering, comforting presence, but an empty space. The stump, barely visible now, still carries the marks of what once was—a life, a friend, a silent witness to my childhood. I remember the day I planted the sapling, the soil clinging to my fingers, the promise I made to watch over it. Now, the air feels a bit cooler, a bit emptier. I keep thinking, it can't be, it just can't be. But the space is there, undeniable.
